investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Scheduler Cannot Place kata.peerpods.io/vm Pods — Insufficient VM Capacity on 2 Eligible Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-05T05:57–06:05Z with an identical Kubernetes FailedScheduling message: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never schedules, the runner never receives a VM ID or a remote state value, so every required evidence field (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent and the expected-output contract is fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on both nodes that are eligible for remote-agent pods. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every new remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state indefinitely. The eval probe times out waiting for the pod to reach a ready state, returns no evidence, and the check fails. This is a cluster-capacity or resource-quota constraint in the production Kubernetes environment, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is currently scoped to this observability eval.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: the cluster has only 2 nodes with this resource, and all available VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 already-saturated nodes. LOWER CONFIDENCE — A recent cluster change (node drain, node removal, or VM-pool resize) that reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously sufficient count to the current 2, without a corresponding reduction in concurrent remote-agent demand.

investigation.title: harness-health Eval Fail: Missing `status` Evidence Due to LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTH_TOKEN Not Configured
investigation.summary: The `harness-health` eval for the `marketplace-bootstrap` feature failed because the harness endpoint at `https://aura-harness-latest.onrender.com` rejected the probe with the error "hosted local harness requires LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTH_TOKEN", causing the API call to return an error object instead of a JSON health payload. As a result, the required evidence key `status` was never populated, violating the contract defined in `infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json`.
investigation.rootCause: The eval runner in `infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs` (lines 1531–1532) calls `GET /api/agents/harness/health` and passes the raw response directly as evidence (`return { evidence: health }`). The harness service at `https://aura-harness-latest.onrender.com` rejected the request because the `LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTH_TOKEN` credential was not present in the eval runner's environment. The rejection response contained `reachable: false`, `url`, and `error` keys but no `status` key, leaving the required evidence field absent and triggering the contract validation failure. This is an eval infrastructure configuration issue — the auth token is missing from the environment in which the scheduled probe runs — not a user-facing product outage.
proof: failed-check.evidence: evidence object contains { reachable: false, url: 'https://aura-harness-latest.onrender.com', latencyMs: 0, error: 'hosted local harness requires LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTH_TOKEN' } — no `status` key is present.
failed-check.message: 'Missing expected evidence: status' confirms the contract validator found `status` absent from the returned evidence.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: contract gap lists `status` as the sole missing required evidence key.
expected-output.contract: check-expectations.json lines 351–358 requires `reachable`, `status`, and `url` with assertions reachable===true, status===200, url nonEmpty.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=145 and evidence.latencyMs=0 confirm the harness call was rejected immediately (auth guard), not a network timeout.

sibling.marketplace-agents: sibling check passed with latencyMs=1222 and evidence key `count`, confirming the broader marketplace-bootstrap feature and production-api environment are reachable — the failure is isolated to the harness-health check.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTH_TOKEN is absent or not injected into the eval runner's environment for the production-api runtime, causing the harness service to reject the probe before returning a health payload with a `status` field.

SECONDARY — The harness service response shape on an auth-rejected request does not include a `status` key, so even if the token were partially misconfigured (e.g., wrong value), the error object returned would still fail the contract.

TERTIARY — The runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1532 passes the raw API response as evidence without normalizing error shapes; if the harness returns an error envelope instead of a health payload, `status` will always be absent regardless of the specific auth failure reason.

investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on both nodes that are eligible for remote-agent pods. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every new remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state indefinitely. The eval probe times out waiting for the pod to reach a ready state, returns no evidence, and the check fails. This is a cluster-capacity or resource-quota constraint in the production Kubernetes environment, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is currently scoped to this observability eval.

investigations.summary: The `harness-health` eval for the `marketplace-bootstrap` feature failed because the harness endpoint at `https://aura-harness-latest.onrender.com` rejected the probe with the error "hosted local harness requires LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTH_TOKEN", causing the API call to return an error object instead of a JSON health payload. As a result, the required evidence key `status` was never populated, violating the contract defined in `infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json`.
investigations.rootCause: The eval runner in `infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs` (lines 1531–1532) calls `GET /api/agents/harness/health` and passes the raw response directly as evidence (`return { evidence: health }`). The harness service at `https://aura-harness-latest.onrender.com` rejected the request because the `LOCAL_HARNESS_AUTH_TOKEN` credential was not present in the eval runner's environment. The rejection response contained `reachable: false`, `url`, and `error` keys but no `status` key, leaving the required evidence field absent and triggering the contract validation failure. This is an eval infrastructure configuration issue — the auth token is missing from the environment in which the scheduled probe runs — not a user-facing product outage.
